question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

He will write a novel next year.
option_1: A novel will have been written by him next year.
option_2: A novel would be written by him next year.
option_3: A novel is going to be written by him next year.
option_4: A novel will be written by him next year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A novel will be written by him next year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The active sentence is in the simple future tense (will write). Passive pattern: Object + will be + V3 + by + agent. (कर्मवाच्य)

 

• Active: "He will write a novel next year." → Passive: "A novel will be written by him next year."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (A novel will have been written by him next year): 'will have been written' is future perfect passive — wrong tense.

 

• Option 2 (A novel would be written by him next year): 'would be written' changes 'will' to 'would' (conditional/past future).

 

• Option 3 (A novel is going to be written by him next year): 'is going to be written' is the passive of 'is going to write' — a different future form.

 

• Future passive: will/shall + be + V3; future perfect passive: will have been + V3.

 

NOTE

 

• The pronoun 'he' becomes 'him' after 'by'.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

We will not open the store until 9 a.m.
option_1: The store will not open until 9 a.m.
option_2: The store is not opened by us until 9 a.m.
option_3: The store would not be opened by us until 9 a.m.
option_4: The store will not be opened by us until 9 a.m.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The store will not be opened by us until 9 a.m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The active sentence is negative simple future: 'will not open'. Passive: Object + will not be + V3 + by + agent. (कर्मवाच्य)

 

• Active: "We will not open the store until 9 a.m." → Passive: "The store will not be opened by us until 9 a.m."
◦  'We' becomes 'us'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The store will not open until 9 a.m): 'will not open' is active (intransitive use); it is not a passive transformation.

 

• Option 2 (The store is not opened by us until 9 a.m): 'is not opened' is simple present passive — wrong tense.

 

• Option 3 (The store would not be opened by us until 9 a.m): 'would not be opened' changes 'will' to 'would'.

 

• Negative passive: the 'not' is placed after the first auxiliary: will not be, is not being, has not been.

 

NOTE

 

• 'by us/by them/by people' is often omitted in real usage, but it must be retained if all options include it.

question:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

Sleep is a vital biological process that restores the body and mind. However, for millions of people worldwide, this natural rhythm is disrupted by sleep disorders. These conditions can range from insomnia, where ____(4)person struggles to fall or stay asleep, to sleepapnea, a potentially serious condition where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep.

 

Chronic sleep problems _______(3) have far-reaching consequences. They impair concentration, weaken the immune system, and increase the risk of conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and depression. The cumulative effect of poor sleep over time can be as harmful as a poor diet or lack of exercise.

 

Causes of sleep disorders vary _____(5). Stress, irregular schedules, excessive screen time before bed, and underlying medical conditions are common triggers. Modern lifestyles, with their relentless pace and constant connectivity, have only worsened the problem.

 

Treatment depends on the underlying cause. For some, improving (1)sleep hygiene such as maintaining a regular sleep schedule, limiting caffeine, and creating a calm bedtime routine can make a significant difference. In more severe cases, medical intervention or therapy may be necessary.

 

Ultimately, addressing sleep disorders is not just about avoiding fatigue it’s about protecting overall health and ensuring that the body’s (2) restorative processes function as they should.

 

The word “restorative” in the passage is closest in meaning to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Healing or renewing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Restorative means having the ability to restore health, strength or well-being; healing or renewing. (पुनर्स्थापक / स्वास्थ्यवर्धक)

 

• The passage begins with 'Sleep is a vital biological process that restores the body and mind', and ends with 'the body's restorative processes' — processes that heal and renew the body.
◦  Hence 'Healing or renewing' is the closest meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Damaging): Damaging is the opposite of restorative.

 

• Option 3 (Weakening): Weakening is also opposite in meaning.

 

• Option 4 (Boring): Boring is unrelated to the context.

 

• Word family: restore (verb), restoration (noun), restorative (adjective). Synonyms: rejuvenating, refreshing, therapeutic, curative.

 

NOTE

 

• In vocabulary-in-context questions, look for the root word used elsewhere in the passage (here, 'restores' in line 1).

solution_text:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

• Sentence types: Simple – one independent clause; Compound – two or more independent clauses; Complex – one independent + one or more dependent clauses; Compound-complex – combination.

 

NOTE

 

• Phrases (participial, infinitive, prepositional) do not change a simple sentence into a complex one.

option_4: It has encouraged people to avoid interacting with pop culture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. It has allowed trends to spread quickly and individuals to participate in shaping pop culture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The last paragraph states: social media platforms 'have made it easier than ever for trends to spread quickly and for individuals to influence pop culture themselves'. (सोशल मीडिया का प्रभाव)

 

• It adds that pop culture is now 'more interactive, fast-paced, and global'.
◦  Option 3 restates this exactly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (It has reduced the popularity of pop culture): 'reduced the popularity' is contradicted — pop culture is more global than ever.

 

• Option 2 (It has made pop culture more difficult to access): 'more difficult to access' is contradicted — social media has made it easier.

 

• Option 4 (It has encouraged people to avoid interacting with pop culture): 'avoid interacting' is contradicted — pop culture is now more interactive.

 

• Factual-question tip: Locate the key word (social media) in the passage and match the option that paraphrases that line.

 

NOTE

 

• Options that contradict the passage can be eliminated immediately.

question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. They built ceremonial plazas and enormous stone temples that are still visible today.

Q. For more than a millennium, the Maya civilisation thrived in Central America.

R. They had a highly developed writing and mathematical system, and their culture was quite advanced.

S. The precise causes of the civilisation's eventual demise are still up for discussion among historians.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Q, P, R, S.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Q introduces the topic — the Maya civilisation thrived in Central America for over a millennium. (तार्किक क्रम)

 

• P ('They built…') and R ('They had…') describe their achievements; S concludes with the debate on the civilisation's eventual demise.
◦  Sequence: Q → P → R → S.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (S, P, R, Q): Begins with the demise — a concluding idea cannot open the paragraph.

 

• Option 3 (P, Q, R, S): Begins with 'They' — the pronoun has no antecedent.

 

• Option 4 (R, P, Q, S): Begins with 'They' — again no antecedent.

 

• Fact: The Maya civilisation flourished in present-day Mexico, Guatemala and Belize and is known for its hieroglyphic script, calendar and the concept of zero.

 

NOTE

 

• Chronological order (origin → achievements → decline) is a common logic in history-based para jumbles.

question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P: This, in turn, resulted in a new appreciation for the simple beauty of nature.

Q: A group of poets in the 19th century began to write about the human experience in a raw, emotional style.

R: Their work, which would later be called Romanticism, moved away from formal, structured verse.

S: They sought to capture the feeling of awe and wonder inspired by mountains and forests.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Q, R, S, P.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Q introduces the subject — a group of 19th-century poets began to write in a raw, emotional style. (तार्किक क्रम)

 

• R ('Their work…') names the movement — Romanticism; S ('They sought…') explains their focus on awe inspired by nature; P ('This, in turn, resulted in…') gives the result.
◦  Sequence: Q → R → S → P.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (P, R, Q, S): 'This, in turn' needs a preceding cause; it cannot open the paragraph.

 

• Option 2 (R, Q, P, S): 'Their work' needs an antecedent (the poets) mentioned earlier.

 

• Option 3 (S, R, P, Q): 'They sought' has no antecedent.

 

• Fact: Romanticism in English poetry began with 'Lyrical Ballads' (1798) by William Wordsworth and S. T. Coleridge.

 

NOTE

 

• Connectors like 'in turn', 'as a result', 'therefore' mark a consequence and come after the cause.

question: What is the antonym of "Superfluous"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Essential.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Superfluous means unnecessary, more than what is needed. (अनावश्यक / फालतू)

 

• Its antonym is Essential — absolutely necessary.
◦  Example: Remove superfluous words from your essay; keep only the essential ones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Excessive): Excessive (more than necessary) is a synonym.

 

• Option 3 (Unnecessary): Unnecessary is a synonym.

 

• Option 4 (Extravagant): Extravagant (exceeding what is reasonable) is closer to a synonym.

 

• Synonyms: redundant, surplus, excess, needless, dispensable. Antonyms: essential, necessary, indispensable, vital, requisite.

 

NOTE

 

• Latin 'super' (over) + 'fluere' (to flow) — 'overflowing', hence surplus.

question: What is the antonym of "Egregious"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Minor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Egregious means outstandingly bad; shocking (e.g., an egregious error). (घोर / अत्यंत बुरा)

 

• Its antonym is Minor — small, unimportant, not serious.
◦  Example: It was an egregious mistake, not a minor slip.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Blatant): Blatant (done openly and unashamedly) is a synonym.

 

• Option 2 (Horrific): Horrific (causing horror) is a synonym in sense.

 

• Option 4 (Appalling): Appalling (shocking, very bad) is a synonym.

 

• Synonyms of egregious: flagrant, glaring, gross, outrageous, blatant. Antonyms: minor, trivial, slight, negligible.

 

NOTE

 

• Etymology: Latin 'e' (out of) + 'grex' (flock) — originally 'standing out from the flock'; today used only in a negative sense.

question:
Which word is nearest in meaning to analysis?

He had a working analysis of mankind’s troubles and was a good judge of character.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Examination.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the sentence, analysis means a detailed examination of something in order to understand it. (विश्लेषण / जाँच)

 

• 'He had a working analysis of mankind's troubles' = he had examined and understood people's problems.
◦  Hence 'Examination' is nearest in meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Illusion): Illusion means a false idea or belief — unrelated.

 

• Option 2 (Doubt): Doubt means uncertainty — unrelated.

 

• Option 3 (Conclusion): Conclusion is the result reached after analysis, not the process of analysis itself.

 

• Synonyms of analysis: examination, study, scrutiny, investigation, evaluation. Antonym: synthesis (combining parts into a whole).

 

NOTE

 

• Plural: analyses; verb: analyse (British) / analyze (American).

question:
Which word is nearest in meaning to regret?

The niece’s tone was one of distinct regret.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sorrow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Regret means a feeling of sadness or disappointment about something that has happened or been done. (पछतावा / खेद)

 

• 'The niece's tone was one of distinct regret' = her tone showed clear sorrow.
◦  Hence 'Sorrow' is nearest in meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Joy): Joy is the opposite of regret.

 

• Option 3 (Celebration): Celebration expresses happiness — opposite in sense.

 

• Option 4 (Relief): Relief is a feeling of reassurance after anxiety — not regret.

 

• Synonyms of regret: remorse, sorrow, repentance, contrition, rue. Antonyms: satisfaction, contentment, joy.

 

NOTE

 

• Regret + gerund (I regret telling him) = sorry about a past action; regret + to-infinitive (We regret to inform you) = sorry about what one is going to say.

question:
Which of the following pairs of words can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

The _____ sorcerer upturned the _____ of poison into the goblet, his lips curling into a smirk.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. vile, vial.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vile (adjective) means extremely unpleasant, wicked; vial (noun) means a small glass bottle for liquids such as medicine or poison. (नीच / शीशी)

 

• "The vile sorcerer upturned the vial of poison into the goblet, his lips curling into a smirk."
◦  An adjective (vile) describes 'sorcerer'; a noun (vial) is needed before 'of poison'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (veil, vail): A veil is a covering for the face; 'vail' is an archaic word (to lower). Neither fits.

 

• Option 2 (vail, veil): 'vail sorcerer' is meaningless and one does not upturn a 'veil' of poison.

 

• Option 3 (vial, vile): The order is reversed — 'vial sorcerer' and 'vile of poison' are wrong.

 

• Homophones: vial/vile (similar sound), veil/vale/vail. Vale = valley.

 

NOTE

 

• A 'phial' is the British spelling of 'vial'.

question:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.

The ________ principle explains the limits of precision for quantum measurements.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Heisenberg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is Heisenberg, after the German physicist Werner Heisenberg, who formulated the Uncertainty Principle (1927). (हाइज़ेनबर्ग अनिश्चितता सिद्धांत)

 

• The principle states that the position and momentum of a particle cannot both be measured with unlimited precision at the same time.
◦  Hence 'The Heisenberg principle explains the limits of precision for quantum measurements.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Heissenberg): 'Heissenberg' – double 's' is wrong.

 

• Option 2 (Hiesenberg): 'Hiesenberg' – the vowels 'e' and 'i' are transposed; the correct order is 'ei'.

 

• Option 4 (Heizenberg): 'Heizenberg' – 'z' replaces 's'; the German pronunciation /z/ misleads here.

 

• Fact: Werner Heisenberg received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1932 for the creation of quantum mechanics.

 

NOTE

 

• German 'ei' is pronounced like English 'eye' (Einstein, Heisenberg).

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitution for the words in italics:

The professor specialized in the study of ancient societies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Archaeology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Archaeology is the study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artefacts — i.e., the study of ancient societies. (पुरातत्व विज्ञान)

 

• The italicised phrase 'study of ancient societies' matches archaeology.
◦  Example: Archaeologists excavated the Harappan sites.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Anthropology): Anthropology is the study of human societies and cultures in general, including living ones — broader than 'ancient societies'.

 

• Option 2 (Sociology): Sociology is the study of present-day society and social behaviour.

 

• Option 4 (Paleontology): Paleontology is the study of fossils of ancient plants and animals (e.g., dinosaurs), not societies.

 

• Related -logies: Numismatics – study of coins; Epigraphy – study of inscriptions; Ethnology – study of races; Philology – study of languages.

 

NOTE

 

• The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was founded in 1861 with Alexander Cunningham as its first Director-General.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. by hedges and trees.

B. The land rose

C. the fields were bordered

D. and fell gently and
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BDCA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• B 'The land rose' begins the sentence (capital letter, subject + verb). D 'and fell gently and' continues the description of the land. (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• C 'the fields were bordered' is the second clause; A 'by hedges and trees.' ends with a full stop.
◦  Sentence: "The land rose and fell gently and the fields were bordered by hedges and trees." → BDCA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (CADB): begins with a lowercase 'the fields'; 'The land rose' cannot come at the end.

 

• Option 3 (ADCB): begins with 'by hedges and trees.', which has a full stop.

 

• Option 4 (DCAB): begins with 'and', a conjunction, and ends with 'The land rose'.

 

• Tips: The part with a capital letter usually begins the sentence; the part with a full stop usually ends it.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Rose and fell' is a pair of opposites used to describe undulating (rolling) land.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. topic around the fire of the

B. I can recall many hours of

C. servants' hall at the end of a day.

D. enjoyable discussion on this
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BDAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• B 'I can recall many hours of' is the opening (capital 'I', subject + verb). D 'enjoyable discussion on this' follows naturally (hours of enjoyable discussion). (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• A 'topic around the fire of the' (on this topic) and C 'servants' hall at the end of a day.' completes it.
◦  Sentence: "I can recall many hours of enjoyable discussion on this topic around the fire of the servants' hall at the end of a day." → BDAC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BADC): 'many hours of topic' is meaningless.

 

• Option 2 (CADB): begins with lowercase 'servants' hall' which ends with a full stop.

 

• Option 4 (CDAB): begins with the concluding part.

 

• Logic: 'on this' needs a noun after it → 'topic'; 'of the' needs a noun after it → 'servants' hall'.

 

NOTE

 

• Look for incomplete endings (of the, on this) and match them with the part that supplies the missing noun.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. kid had an unnerving way of emphasizing certain words

B. shoulder to the left.

C. Archie noted the

D. by moving his head in a wide circular movement from the right
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. CADB.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C 'Archie noted the' opens the sentence (proper noun subject + verb). A 'kid had an unnerving way of emphasizing certain words' completes 'the … kid'. (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• D 'by moving his head in a wide circular movement from the right' describes how; B 'shoulder to the left.' ends it.
◦  Sentence: "Archie noted the kid had an unnerving way of emphasizing certain words by moving his head in a wide circular movement from the right shoulder to the left." → CADB.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (CDAB): 'noted the by moving' is meaningless.

 

• Option 3 (ACDB): begins with lowercase 'kid', which needs 'the' before it.

 

• Option 4 (ADCB): begins with 'kid' and places 'Archie noted the' in the middle illogically.

 

• Logic: 'from the right' naturally pairs with 'shoulder to the left' (from … to).

 

NOTE

 

• Correlative prepositional pairs (from … to, between … and) help link parts in jumbled sentences.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. to disturb him, seized his telephone and had almost

B. He dashed back across the road, hurried up to

C. finished dialing his home number when he changed his mind.

D. his office, snapped at his secretary not
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BDAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• B 'He dashed back across the road, hurried up to' opens the sentence. D 'his office, snapped at his secretary not' continues (hurried up to his office). (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• A 'to disturb him, seized his telephone and had almost' (not to disturb him) and C 'finished dialing his home number when he changed his mind.' ends it.
◦  Sequence: BDAC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BADC): 'hurried up to to disturb him' is ungrammatical.

 

• Option 2 (CDAB): begins with the concluding part.

 

• Option 4 (CADB): begins with the concluding part.

 

• Logic: 'snapped at his secretary not' + 'to disturb him' forms the negative infinitive 'not to disturb'.

 

NOTE

 

• A series of actions by the same subject follows chronological order: dashed → hurried → snapped → seized → had almost finished.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. glasses exactly the shape of the

B. markings the cat had had around its eyes.

C. severe-looking woman who was wearing square

D. Instead he was smiling at a rather
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DCAB.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• D 'Instead he was smiling at a rather' opens the sentence. C 'severe-looking woman who was wearing square' follows (a rather severe-looking woman). (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• A 'glasses exactly the shape of the' (square glasses) and B 'markings the cat had had around its eyes.' completes it.
◦  Sequence: DCAB.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (DACB): 'a rather glasses' is meaningless.

 

• Option 2 (CADB): begins with lowercase 'severe-looking woman'.

 

• Option 3 (BCDA): begins with the concluding part.

 

• Logic: 'a rather' needs an adjective → 'severe-looking'; 'square' needs a noun → 'glasses'.

 

NOTE

 

• 'had had' is the past perfect of 'have' — grammatically correct.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. the responsibility which ultimately lies with

B. ourselves, it has to be said that certain employers

C. have done much to encourage these sorts of trends.

D. Though we must be careful not to attempt to deny
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DABC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• D 'Though we must be careful not to attempt to deny' opens the subordinate clause. A 'the responsibility which ultimately lies with' supplies the object of 'deny'. (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• B 'ourselves, it has to be said that certain employers' and C 'have done much to encourage these sorts of trends.' complete the sentence.
◦  Sequence: DABC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (DBAC): 'deny ourselves' changes the meaning, and 'employers the responsibility' is illogical.

 

• Option 2 (DCBA): 'deny have done much' is ungrammatical.

 

• Option 3 (DACB): 'lies with have done much' is ungrammatical.

 

• Logic: 'lies with' needs a pronoun/noun → 'ourselves'; 'certain employers' needs a verb → 'have done much'.

 

NOTE

 

• A 'Though' clause is followed by a main clause separated by a comma.

question:
Arrange the sentences into a coherent paragraph:

A. The learner became self-directed.

B. Curiosity was nurtured early.

C. Exploration was encouraged.

D. Independent thinking developed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BCDA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentences describe a learner's development: B Curiosity was nurtured early → C Exploration was encouraged → D Independent thinking developed → A The learner became self-directed. (तार्किक क्रम)

 

• The order moves from cause (early curiosity) to the final result (self-direction).
◦  Sequence: BCDA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BCAD): becoming self-directed (final result) cannot come before independent thinking develops.

 

• Option 3 (DCBA): reverses the natural order of development.

 

• Option 4 (CBDA): exploration before curiosity is illogical.

 

• Logic: Process-based jumbles follow a cause-and-effect chain from the earliest stage to the final outcome.

 

NOTE

 

• The sentence that expresses the final outcome/conclusion usually comes last.

question:
Arrange the sentences into a coherent paragraph:

A. This imbalance affects both physical and mental health.

B. Long working hours reduce time for personal life.

C. Work-life balance is often ignored today.

D. Stress levels increase due to constant pressure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CBDA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C introduces the topic — 'Work-life balance is often ignored today.' (तार्किक क्रम)

 

• B gives the cause (long working hours), D the effect (stress increases), and A the conclusion ('This imbalance affects both physical and mental health').
◦  Sequence: CBDA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (BCDA): begins with a specific cause instead of the general topic.

 

• Option 3 (CDBA): stress (effect) comes before long working hours (cause).

 

• Option 4 (BDCA): the topic sentence C appears in the middle.

 

• Logic: General statement → cause → effect → conclusion ('This imbalance' refers back to all preceding ideas).

 

NOTE

 

• Demonstratives like 'This imbalance' refer to something already stated, so they cannot begin the paragraph.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Breathe.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is Breathe — the verb meaning to take air into the lungs and let it out. (साँस लेना)

 

• 'Breath' (noun) is the air taken in; 'breathe' (verb) is the action.
◦  Example: Take a deep breath and breathe slowly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Breth): 'Breth' – the 'a' is missing (correct: breath).

 

• Option 3 (Briliant): 'Briliant' – double 'l' is required (correct: brilliant).

 

• Option 4 (Bruize): 'Bruize' – 's' is required, not 'z' (correct: bruise).

 

• Noun–verb pairs: breath/breathe, bath/bathe, cloth/clothe, loath (adj.)/loathe (v).

 

NOTE

 

• The final 'e' in verbs like breathe, bathe, clothe changes the 'th' sound from /θ/ to /ð/.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Captain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is Captain — a person who leads a team, ship or military unit. (कप्तान)

 

• It ends in -ain (cap-tain).
◦  Example: The captain led the team to victory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Berglar): 'Berglar' – correct spelling is 'burglar'.

 

• Option 2 (Campain): 'Campain' – the silent 'g' is missing (correct: campaign).

 

• Option 4 (Carefull): 'Carefull' – the suffix '-ful' has a single 'l' (correct: careful).

 

• Suffix rule: full → -ful (careful, beautiful, hopeful); but 'fully' in adverbs (carefully).

 

NOTE

 

• Silent 'g' words: campaign, foreign, sovereign, reign, design, benign.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To bury the hatchet
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To make peace.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• To bury the hatchet means to make peace or end a quarrel. (सुलह करना / बैर भुलाना)

 

• Origin: Native American custom of burying weapons (hatchets) when making peace.
◦  Example: After years of rivalry, the two brothers decided to bury the hatchet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (To start a fight): 'To start a fight' is the opposite.

 

• Option 3 (To dig a hole): 'To dig a hole' is a literal interpretation.

 

• Option 4 (To hide a weapon): 'To hide a weapon' is again literal.

 

• Similar idioms: Smoke the peace pipe; Let bygones be bygones; Mend fences; Make up.

 

NOTE

 

• Opposite idiom: 'to take up the cudgels' (to start fighting or defending strongly).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To go to the dogs
option_2: To decline in condition or quality
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To decline in condition or quality.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• To go to the dogs means to decline in condition or quality; to deteriorate or be ruined. (बर्बाद हो जाना / पतन होना)

 

• Example: The once-famous hotel has gone to the dogs due to poor management.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (To be successful): 'To be successful' is the opposite.

 

• Option 3 (To get along well): 'To get along well' refers to friendly relations — unrelated.

 

• Option 4 (To become an animal lover): 'To become an animal lover' is a literal misreading.

 

• Similar idioms: go downhill, go to pot, go to rack and ruin, go to seed.

 

NOTE

 

• Related dog idioms: let sleeping dogs lie (avoid stirring up old problems); a dog in the manger (a selfish person).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To have too many irons in the fire
option_2: To be involved in too many activities at once
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To be involved in too many activities at once.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• To have too many irons in the fire means to be involved in too many activities or projects at once. (एक साथ बहुत सारे काम हाथ में लेना)

 

• Origin: a blacksmith who heated too many irons at a time could not work on all of them properly.
◦  Example: He has too many irons in the fire to do any job well.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (To be very focused): 'To be very focused' is the opposite.

 

• Option 3 (To be lazy): 'To be lazy' is the opposite of being overly busy.

 

• Option 4 (To be a blacksmith): 'To be a blacksmith' is a literal interpretation.

 

• Similar idioms: spread oneself too thin; bite off more than one can chew; have one's hands full.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Strike while the iron is hot' – act at the right moment (also from blacksmithing).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To flog a dead horse
option_1: To revive interest in a subject
option_2: To waste effort on a lost cause
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To waste effort on a lost cause.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• To flog a dead horse means to waste effort on a lost cause — on something that has no chance of success. (व्यर्थ प्रयास करना)

 

• Example: Arguing with him is flogging a dead horse; he will never change his mind.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information
